Read out of saint.gr's line for 2 Ιουλίου, «Άγιος Ιουβενάλιος Πατριάρχης Ιεροσολύμων», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 2. јул ст. ст., „Св. Јувеналије патријарх Јерусалимски“ — Св. is not a rank, „патријарх“ is the rank, which `types` already carries, and „Јерусалимски“ is the see that rank governs and comes off with it, exactly as the folder’s Romanian and Greek forms were taken «with the rank word and the see left off». The bare forename is what the heading leaves, and «of Jerusalem» in the display name is the corpus’s own. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Јувеналије», so there is no fold — worth having measured, the corpus keeping a `juvenal-of-alaska` and a `juvenal-of-narni` whom `sr-namesweep.mjs` prints directly beneath this man.

The calendar’s own nominative from name link 1130, «Святитель Иувеналий (Ювеналий) Иерусалимский, патриарх», with the rank word at the head and the rank word after the comma left off. The parenthesis is the calendar’s second spelling of the forename and not a surname; it is kept because the page prints it, as the corpus’s other parenthesised epithets are. The day’s own line gives the name in the genitive and with the other grade, «Свт. Иувеналия , архиеп. Иерусалимского». `fk.mjs` returns no holder for the form, nor for it with the parenthesis dropped.

floruit.note: doxologia.ro: «Sfântul Iuvenalie a fost Patriarhul Ierusalimului între anii 420 și 458». The page gives neither a year of birth nor a year of death.

death.note: The folder’s first year of death, and two books give it one year apart, so it is widened rather than chosen. saint.gr dates his death, on the word of Dositheos, to 457. The Охридски пролог for 2. јул ст. ст.: „у дубокој старости представи се Господу, 458. год.“ — in deep old age he presented himself to the Lord in the year 458. doxologia gives no year of death at all, only the interval of the patriarchate recorded under `floruit`. Deep old age is not a birth and none is written. The thirty-eight years this book gives for the tenure are a duration and not a date, and nothing is subtracted from 458 to reach a first year, though it would have agreed with doxologia’s 420 (5 October 2026).

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 2 July is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **A FIRST `death`, AND IT IS WIDENED IN THE SAME BREATH THAT MAKES IT.** The folder held `floruit` 420 to 458 `attested` off doxologia’s «Sfântul Iuvenalie a fost Patriarhul Ierusalimului între anii 420 și 458» and **no `death` at all**; doxologia gives neither birth nor death, and saint.gr dates the death, on the word of Dositheos, to 457. This book says „у дубокој старости представи се Господу, 458. год.“ — in deep old age he presented himself to the Lord in the year 458. One year apart, and the rule widens rather than chooses: `death` earliest 457, latest 458, display «457 or 458», basis traditional, both sentences in the note. The `floruit` is passed back **verbatim**, note and all, because `upgrade.py` replaces the whole `dates` object and a field not retyped exactly would be a silent edit; its remark that doxologia gives no year of death is still true of doxologia. **Deep old age is not a birth** and none is written. **THE 38 YEARS ARE REFUSED, AND SO IS THE SUBTRACTION THAT WOULD HAVE AGREED WITH THE FOLDER.** „38 година управљаше Јувеналије црквом Јерусалимском као њен јерарх“ — thirty-eight years. That is a duration and not a date, it is written nowhere as a number of years in a field, and **nothing is subtracted from 458 to reach a first year**, though the result would have landed on the 420 the folder already holds. A year derived by arithmetic is refused however well it agrees. The three books now give three figures for the tenure — this book’s 38, doxologia’s interval, and saint.gr’s «twenty-eight unbroken years» — and all three are prose. WHAT IS NEW, AND IT IS MOST OF A LIFE THE OTHER TWO BOOKS DID NOT TELL. The folder had the two Councils as bare attendances. This book names what he fought at each: at Ephesus Nestorius, „који је Богородицу називао Христородицом“, who called the Theotokos Christotokos; at Chalcedon Eutyches and Dioscorus, who taught that in Christ there was one nature only, the divine, without the human. And then the whole of a deposition and a restoration that nothing in the folder hinted at: that the heresies were condemned but the heretics not rooted out; that by the intrigue and violence of a Theodosius, a friend of Dioscorus, Juvenal was driven from his throne and that Theodosius raised himself to his place; that the empress Eudocia, widow of Theodosius the Younger and then settled in Jerusalem, at first helped the usurper; that she went at last to [Symeon the Stylite](/saints/symeon-the-stylite) to ask where the truth lay, was shown every heretical teaching for what it was, repented, and turned against the false patriarch; and that a letter came from the emperor to the commander Athanasius to drive Theodosius out and restore Juvenal, which he shortly did. **AND ONE MORE THING, WHICH IS NOT A DATE EITHER.** „У време св. Јувеналија утврђено je празновање Божића 25. децембра“ — in his time the keeping of the Nativity on 25 December was established. That is a day in the church year and not a year in a life; it goes in the life and into no field. `types` UNTOUCHED: `hierarch` and `patriarch` are both there, „патријарх“ is the `patriarch` and „као њен јерарх“ the `hierarch`; Свети is not a rank. `office` UNTOUCHED at «Patriarch» — „Јерусалимски“ is the see and the folder’s own display name carries it; no `office` string is invented. No `locations`: Jerusalem, Ephesus and Chalcedon in a narrative are not a coordinate. **THE ROWS, AND THE FIVE REFUSED.** The folder already relates `euthymius-the-great`, `symeon-the-stylite`, `gerasimus-of-the-jordan` and `agapius-disciple-of-passarion`, and this book’s own first sentence names the first three among the great lights of the Church whose contemporary he was, so the three are named in the new prose as the folder’s older prose already names them. **No new row is added and five are refused.** „Теодосија“ in that same list is **not** written as `theodosius-the-cenobiarch`: an identification made off a name in another man’s life is not an identification, and this entry holds **two different Theodosii besides** — the usurping patriarch and the emperor Theodosius the Younger — which is reason enough to name none of them in the prose by a form that matches a folder. **Eudocia takes no row** though `eudocia-the-empress`’s display name is «Eudocia, wife of Theodosius the Younger» and this book calls her the widow of Theodosius the Younger in those words: an emperor or an empress in a life is not automatically a relation, and the match is again an identification off a name. **Pulcheria takes no row** on the same ground, `pulcheria-the-empress` existing. **Nestorius, Eutyches and Dioscorus take no rows**: `ls saints | grep -i nestorius` holds nobody, and `eutyches-the-hieromartyr` is «Eutyches, disciple of John the Theologian» while the three Dioscori of the corpus are martyrs of other centuries — a heresiarch is not the saint who shares his name, and the prose names all three plainly for that reason. **The commander Athanasius takes no row**, thirty-odd folders carrying that name and none of them this officer. **A Council is not a folder.** **AND TWO OF THOSE REFUSALS WERE MADE IN THE NOTE BECAUSE `npm test` CAUGHT THEM IN THE PROSE — §6’s TRAP MEASURED TWICE IN ONE PARAGRAPH.** The first draft read «the empress Eudocia, widow of Theodosius the Younger, who had settled in Jerusalem» and «she went at last to Symeon the Stylite to ask him where the truth was», and `related-floor.test.mjs` failed 483/2 on the **reverse** direction of both: `theodosius-the-younger -> juvenal-of-jerusalem` and `symeon-the-stylite -> juvenal-of-jerusalem`. `theodosius-the-younger` is a folder and «Theodosius the Younger» is its display name exactly, which is how an emperor named only to date a widow became a claimed relation. Symeon is the sharper half: the folder **already relates him** and the older prose already names him in a markdown link, which passes — and a **second, unlinked** mention of the same display name in the same life does not, the reverse row not existing on `symeon-the-stylite`. So the forward row is not what the test wanted. The fix was §6’s both times — the name out of the prose and into this note — applied as a `life_replace`-only spec, `.tmp/sr-drafts/fix-07-02.json`, with the same two changes made in the day’s generator so that the generator still reproduces the folder, and this row then re-applied with `.tmp/sr-reapply-json.py`, which touches the json half only. **Nothing was added to `scripts/related-floor-exclusions.json`.** The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FIRST ENTRY IS A FEAST AND TAKES NO FOLDER AND NO ROW. „Положење ризе пресвете Богородице у цркву Влахернску у Цариграду“ — the Deposition of the Robe of the most holy Theotokos in the church of Blachernae at Constantinople. §5 is explicit that a „Празник“ is not a folder, and this heading names no person at all. **The two men its body names get no row on that ground alone**: „Галвије и Кандид“, two patricians of Constantinople who lodged at Nazareth in the house of a Jewish maiden keeping the Robe in a secret chamber, took the relic and brought it to the City. A row’s quoted line is the Prologue’s own heading, whole — the ruling two men martyred by name inside a body were refused rows on, on 18 June — and this heading is a feast. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Галвије» and `candidus-of-the-forty-martyrs` for «Кандид», who is one of the Forty of Sebaste and not a patrician of the fifth century; `ls saints | grep -i galbius` holds nobody. So **no folder for either, and the maiden of Nazareth is unnamed in the book itself.** The rest of the entry’s people are refused with it: the emperor Leo and the empress Verina, the patriarch Gennadius, and the emperor Marcian and Pulcheria who built the church — emperors and a patriarch in a feast’s narrative, and `verina` holds nobody; and **the regnal years „(458- 471.)“ this book gives for Leo are written nowhere**, an unbounded reign being refused and an emperor being no source for a year in any case. The Scythian commander Vlahern, after whom the bay and the church are named and who was killed there, is an etymology and not a person this corpus keeps.

hymns.tone: Ἦχος πλ. α'. Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον.
hymns.text: Τῆς Σιὼν ἱεράρχην, Ἰουβενάλιον, Ὀρθοδοξίας τὸ κλέος καὶ φρυκτωρὸν τῶν πιστῶν, εὐφημήσωμεν λαμπρῶς, καὶ ἀνυμνήσωμεν· ὅτι ἐφύλαξε πιστῶς τῶν δογμάτων θησαυρόν, παλαίσας κατὰ τῆς πλάνης· καὶ ἔλαβεν ἐκ τοῦ Λόγου, στεφάνους δόξης ἐν τῇ ἄνω Σιών.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α', Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον, on the page of «Άγιος Ιουβενάλιος Πατριάρχης Ιεροσολύμων»

english.text: Let us brightly praise and hymn Juvenal, hierarch of Sion, the glory of Orthodoxy and beacon of the faithful; for he faithfully guarded the treasure of the doctrines, wrestling against error, and received from the Word the crowns of glory in the Sion above.

hymns.text: Τῆς Σιωνίτιδος τὸν πρόεδρον τιμήσωμεν, τῶν ὀρθοδόξων τὸν φρουρὸν καὶ θεῖον φύλακα, τὸν συντρίψαντα αἱρέσων μένος πλάνης· ἀνεδείχθης τῶν Πατέρων ἰσοστάσιος, καὶ μεγάλων θεολόγων τὸ ἀντίγραφον· ὅθεν κράζομεν· Χαῖρε Ἰουβενάλιε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ', Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ, on the page of «Άγιος Ιουβενάλιος Πατριάρχης Ιεροσολύμων»

english.text: Let us honour the president of the church of Sion, the guard and divine keeper of the Orthodox, who broke the fury of heresy's error. You were shown to be the equal of the Fathers and the copy of the great theologians; wherefore we cry: Rejoice, Juvenal.

hymns.text: Брата Божия на престоле архиерейства преемниче,/ святаго града Иерусалима иерарше достохвальне,/ с богомудрыми отцы в Халкидоне изъяснил еси воплощение Сына Божия,/ пришедшаго мир обновити и обожити вся человеки,/ в Церкви Его с Ним сочетавшаяся,/ святителю отче Иувеналие,/ предстоя ныне во Царствии Отца светов,/ о почитающих тя любовию молися,/ да мир и милость Спасова будет с нами.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 2 июля ст. ст., «Тропарь святителя Иувеналия, патриарха Иерусалимского», глас 4 — his own and not a common: it names him, names his see, and names the council of Chalcedon at which the calendar has him speak

english.text: O successor upon the throne of the hierarchy of the Brother of God, praiseworthy hierarch of the holy city of Jerusalem, with the God-wise fathers at Chalcedon thou didst set forth the incarnation of the Son of God, who came to renew the world and to deify all men who are joined to him in his Church. O hierarch and father Juvenal, standing now in the kingdom of the Father of lights, pray for those who honour thee with love, that the peace and the mercy of the Saviour may be with us.
